newsitem.title: FINLAND: MARKKA FLOAT MORE NATURAL THAN ERM II - ESKO HELLE.
newsitem.headline: MARKKA FLOAT MORE NATURAL THAN ERM II - ESKO HELLE.

text.p: Leftist Alliance parliamentary group chairman Esko Helle said on Tuesday a floating markka would be a more natural option than ERM II if Finland did not join Europe's planned single currency from day one in 1999.
Helle said a government report on EMU did not pay sufficient attention to the float option.
"It (a float) would be a more natural alternative to ERM II ... A float must be regarded as a serious option," Helle told parliament during a debate on the government's EMU report.
In the report, the five-party coalition said a float would not be in line with government policy.

Earlier, Social Democratic Party parliamentary group chairman Erkki Tuomioja told the house a float should be considered as an option to pegging the markka to ERM II if Finland did not join the third stage of EMU in the first group.
The SDP and the Leftist Alliance are part of the left-right-green coalition, whose stated goal is that Finland should join monetary union from the beginning in 1999.
Helle said his parliamentary group's final stance would be decided only later.
He agreed with Tuomioja that parliament's decision on Finnish EMU membership -- due early in 1998 -- should be based on a bill proposed by the government, rather than on a notification.
